$comment: AIF-C01 question bank, authored at S4 (exam-author) per methodology/03-authoring-guide.md, clean-room from concepts.json + authoring.json + derivation artefacts only. Every concept is the primary concept of exactly one item; each wrong option carries a distinct distractor pattern (registry D01-D20 + extensions E01-E05); rationales are option-keyed in canonical vocabulary. Locale en-US per manifest.

questions.question: A video game publisher's AI roadmap lists three initiatives: a fraud-scoring model for in-game purchases, an image generator for concept art, and a dialogue assistant that plans multi-step quests and calls game-engine tools. The CTO wants the roadmap slide to group each initiative inside its parent field. Which grouping is correct?

options.A: Machine learning sits inside AI, deep learning sits inside machine learning and is built on neural networks; the image generator belongs to generative AI, a newer branch built on deep learning, and the tool-calling quest assistant belongs to agentic AI
options.B: Deep learning is the umbrella field, machine learning is one technique inside it, and both generative AI and agentic AI sit inside machine learning as its two modern sub-branches
options.C: Generative AI and agentic AI have superseded machine learning, so the fraud-scoring model should be migrated to a generative approach before the roadmap is drawn at all
options.D: The three initiatives should be grouped under a single AI label, because the boundaries between these fields shift too quickly for the distinctions to be worth mapping

rationale.correct: The field nests: machine learning is a subset of AI, deep learning is a subset of machine learning built on neural networks, and generative AI and agentic AI are newer branches that build on that stack rather than standing beside it. A language model earns the label large language model through parameter and training-data scale, and an assistant that plans and calls tools is the agentic AI case. The fraud model is classic machine learning; the concept-art generator is generative AI; the quest assistant is agentic AI.

distractors.B: This inverts the containment: deep learning is the subset that lives inside machine learning, not the umbrella above it. Swapping the two neighboring terms produces a hierarchy that reads plausibly and is wrong at every level.
distractors.C: Newer branches do not supersede the fields they grew from. Generative AI builds on deep learning; a fraud-scoring problem with labeled purchase data remains a standard machine learning fit, and migrating it buys nothing.
distractors.D: Flattening the fields into one label discards exactly the structure the roadmap needs: the three initiatives require different data, different skills, and different risk controls, and those differences follow the hierarchy.

questions.question: A dairy processing plant runs a system that predicts spoilage risk for each production batch. A gradient-boosting procedure learned from three years of historical batch readings; every night the resulting system scores the day's new readings. During handover, a new engineer reads four claims in the runbook. Which claim is accurate?

options.A: The gradient-boosting algorithm is the procedure that learned from the historical readings during training; the model is the artifact that procedure produced, and the nightly scoring of new readings is inferencing
options.B: The model and the algorithm are the same object referred to at different times: before deployment the team calls it an algorithm, and after deployment the same thing is called a model
options.C: The nightly scoring run is a form of training, because the system is exposed to new batch readings each night and therefore continues to learn from them
options.D: Because the system keeps inferencing in production, it gradually improves its own weights with every prediction it makes, without any retraining step

rationale.correct: The four working parts separate cleanly: the algorithm is the procedure that learns, the model is the artifact it produces, training is the phase that learns from historical data, and inferencing is the phase that predicts on new input. Here the gradient-boosting algorithm ran once over three years of readings during training, produced a model, and that model performs inferencing every night.

distractors.B: Algorithm and model are different kinds of thing, not one thing renamed over time: the procedure exists before and after training, and the model is the separate artifact the procedure produced from data.
distractors.C: Seeing new data is not learning from it. The nightly run is inferencing: the model predicts on new readings without its parameters changing. Training is the distinct phase in which parameters are learned.
distractors.D: Inferencing does not update a model. A deployed model's parameters stay fixed between training runs; improvement requires an explicit retraining step, not the act of predicting.

questions.question: A used-car marketplace holds 40,000 historical listings, each labeled with the final sale price the vehicle achieved. The product team wants to predict the likely sale price of every new listing at the moment it is posted. Which learning approach fits the data and the required output?

options.A: Supervised learning trained on the labeled listings, framed as regression, because the supervision signal exists and the required output is a continuous price
options.B: Unsupervised learning that clusters similar listings, with each new listing priced at the average of the cluster it lands in
options.C: Reinforcement learning that rewards the system each time a seller accepts a suggested price, so the pricing policy improves through interaction
options.D: Supervised learning framed as classification into low, medium, and high price bands, since bands are simpler to report than exact figures

rationale.correct: Two signals decide the approach: the 40,000 listings carry labels, so this is supervised learning rather than unsupervised learning, and the output is a continuous number, which makes it regression rather than classification or clustering. Labeled data plus a numeric target is the textbook regression setup.

distractors.B: Clustering is the unsupervised move for unlabeled data. Discarding 40,000 existing price labels to group listings by similarity throws away the supervision signal that makes a direct prediction possible.
distractors.C: A reward loop adds interactive machinery the problem does not have: the historical labels already state the right answer for every training example, so nothing needs to be discovered through trial and interaction.
distractors.D: Collapsing a continuous price into three bands removes the precision the team asked for. Classification is for categorical targets; when the target is a number, regression keeps the information the bands would flatten away.

questions.question: A courier delivery network scores roughly 2 million parcel records for misdelivery risk. The scores feed an operations dashboard that supervisors review each morning at 6 a.m.; the input is the previous day's complete manifest, and no scoring requests occur during the day. The three-person data team wants minimal operational load. How should the model be served?

options.A: Run batch inference over the nightly manifest through a managed API service, since the workload's volume and latency shape needs no always-on endpoint and the provider carries the operational responsibility
options.B: Provision a real-time inference endpoint that stays available around the clock, so the dashboard reflects each parcel the moment its record is created
options.C: Self-host the model behind the team's own API on dedicated servers, keeping full control of the serving stack in-house where the team can tune it
options.D: Submit each parcel record individually to an asynchronous inference queue with callbacks, collecting the responses as they complete overnight

rationale.correct: Inference mode follows the workload's latency and volume shape: 2 million records arriving as one nightly manifest, consumed once each morning, is the defining batch profile. Choosing a managed API service over a self-hosted API decides who carries the operational responsibility, and a three-person team that wants minimal load should let the provider carry it.

distractors.B: An always-on real-time endpoint serves workloads that must answer individual requests within moments. Nothing here is consumed before 6 a.m., so around-the-clock availability is capacity the dashboard can never use, paid for continuously.
distractors.C: Full control is a comfort criterion, not a requirement this workload states. A self-hosted API transfers patching, scaling, and availability onto the same three people who asked for minimal operational load.
distractors.D: Asynchronous inference fits individual long-running requests that need a response later. Submitting 2 million records one at a time with callbacks rebuilds a batch job out of queue machinery, with more moving parts and no gain.

questions.question: An electric utility collects two feeds for a transformer-failure project: substation sensor readings recorded every 30 seconds with a timestamp, exported as CSV tables, and free-text maintenance notes typed by field crews. An architect must characterize the data before selecting techniques. Which characterization is right?

options.A: The sensor feed is time-series data that is structured, and the maintenance notes are text data that is unstructured; modality and structure are different properties, so the CSV export does not make the problem tabular
options.B: The sensor feed is tabular data, because anything delivered in rows and columns is tabular, and the ordering of the rows is a storage detail rather than a property of the data
options.C: Both feeds should be treated as one dataset of a single type, since the distinction between the feeds has no consequence for how models consume them
options.D: Both feeds are unstructured until a schema is applied to them during feature engineering, at which point each becomes structured data

rationale.correct: A dataset's type and its structure are read separately. Readings ordered by timestamp every 30 seconds are time-series data: the temporal ordering is the property that modeling must respect, and it survives any file format. The sensor feed is structured; the free-text notes are text data and unstructured. Conflating modality with structure, or either with the export format, leads straight to the wrong technique.

distractors.B: The CSV rows and columns are the container, not the type. When the ordering by timestamp carries the signal, treating the feed as plain tabular data invites techniques that shuffle away exactly what predicts a failure.
distractors.C: Merging a structured time-series feed with unstructured text erases the distinction that drives technique choice: the two modalities need different preparation, and a single undifferentiated dataset serves neither.
distractors.D: Structure is a property the data has now, not a status conferred by a later pipeline stage. The sensor readings are already structured, and applying a schema to free text does not happen as a side effect of feature engineering.

questions.question: A payroll services bureau is deciding whether to build an ML system that computes statutory tax withholding for every paycheck it processes. A feasibility review, including a cost-benefit analysis, produced five findings. Which TWO findings should steer the bureau toward a conventional rules-based implementation instead? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Withholding amounts are fully determined by published tax tables, and any deviation from those tables is a compliance defect
options.B: The projected cost of building, hosting, and monitoring the model exceeds the annual savings it could produce over a maintained rules engine
options.C: The engineering team does not currently operate a GPU cluster capable of training a model of this kind
options.D: A vendor demonstration the team attended produced visible errors on two of the sample paychecks it processed
options.E: Client payroll records contain personal information, and personal information is not permitted to be processed by machine learning systems

rationale.correct: AI earns its cost where it assists human decision making, scales a solution, or automates judgment, and it is the wrong choice when a deterministic answer is required or the cost-benefit analysis fails. Both disqualifiers are present: a calculation fully determined by published tables is not a prediction problem, since any deviation is a defect rather than an acceptable error, and the review shows the model costing more than the value it returns over a rules engine.

distractors.C: What hardware the team happens to own is a criterion from outside the decision framework: compute can be rented in an afternoon, and a finding about current resources says nothing about whether prediction fits the task.
distractors.D: Two visible errors in one vendor demonstration is an anecdote, not measurement. A demo's sample proves nothing in either direction, and decisions steered by it would be steered by noise.
distractors.E: This states a compliance rule that does not exist in this form: personal data can be processed by ML systems under appropriate controls. The real disqualifiers are the deterministic requirement and the failed economics, not a blanket prohibition.

questions.question: A home security monitoring company wants to estimate next month's false-alarm volume for each neighborhood it serves, using three years of alarm history, so it can roster response staff ahead of demand. Before any service is shortlisted, the team must name the AI application category this capability belongs to. Which category is it?

options.A: Forecasting, because the system predicts a future quantity from patterns in historical, time-ordered alarm data
options.B: Fraud detection, because false alarms are deceptive events and the system's purpose is to identify where deception is likely
options.C: Computer vision, deployed on the camera streams to detect and tally alarm events in real time so volumes can be derived from the tallies
options.D: Classification, labeling each neighborhood as either high risk or low risk so the roster can be planned from two simple categories

rationale.correct: Naming the application category comes before any service is chosen, and the category is read from what the capability produces: a future quantity estimated from time-ordered history is forecasting. Neighboring categories such as fraud detection, computer vision, or recommendation systems describe different capabilities, and the roster decision needs a number per neighborhood per month, which is exactly what forecasting yields.

distractors.B: The word false in false alarm suggests deception, but nothing here identifies deceptive actors or transactions. Fraud detection flags individual suspicious events; this capability estimates an aggregate future volume.
distractors.C: Building a real-time vision pipeline to count events is heavy machinery for a number the alarm history already contains. Three years of recorded volumes answer the question without analyzing a single video frame.
distractors.D: Two risk labels flatten the quantity the rostering decision needs. Staffing ahead of demand requires how many, not which of two buckets, and the flattening discards most of what the history can predict.

questions.question: A boutique hotel group is adding AI capabilities across its guest services and must pick the AWS service that performs each job. For each requirement below, select the service. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Convert recorded front-desk phone calls into searchable text so shift supervisors can review what was said.
Render each guest's nightly itinerary as natural-sounding speech for the in-room voice assistant to read aloud.
Detect sentiment and extract key phrases from thousands of free-text guest review comments.
Convert the housekeeping app's status messages from English into the other languages the staff read.
Turn voicemail messages left on the concierge line into text for the morning triage queue.

rationale.correct: Each task-level managed service performs one job, and the direction of the task separates near neighbors. Speech becoming text is Amazon Transcribe, which covers both the front-desk recordings and the concierge voicemail. Text becoming speech is the opposite direction, which is Amazon Polly reading the itinerary aloud. Understanding what text means, including sentiment and key phrases in the review comments, is Amazon Comprehend. Moving text between languages is Amazon Translate. The pair to hold apart is Transcribe and Polly: both involve speech, and the arrow between speech and text points in opposite directions.

questions.question: A commercial drone inspection firm detects corrosion defects on remote transmission towers. Flights happen far outside network coverage, the pilot must see flagged defects during the flight to re-photograph them, and the energy regulator requires the firm to account for why each defect was flagged. The imagery workload feels like a fit for the newest foundation models. What should the firm deploy?

options.A: A compact traditional ML vision model running on the drone's onboard hardware, because the operational constraints and explainability requirements dominate this choice rather than raw model capability
options.B: A multimodal foundation model accessed through a cloud API, with each flight's imagery uploaded for scoring after the drone returns to network coverage
options.C: A foundation model hosted on a GPU server carried in the ground-support vehicle, streaming frames from the drone over a dedicated local radio link
options.D: A foundation model fine-tuned on the firm's corrosion imagery, since fine-tuning on domain data makes the model's decisions explainable to the regulator

rationale.correct: When regulatory concerns, explainability requirements, or operational constraints dominate, a traditional ML model or small model beats a foundation model regardless of headline capability. Every stated requirement points that way: offline flight rules out API calls, in-flight results rule out deferred scoring, and the regulator's demand to account for each flag favors a simpler model whose decisions can be explained. Foundation models earn their place when those constraints are absent.

distractors.B: Uploading after the flight postpones scoring past the moment it is needed: the pilot must re-photograph flagged defects while still airborne. Deferred results quietly convert an in-flight capability into a next-day report.
distractors.C: A GPU vehicle and a dedicated radio link add an infrastructure project to every flight in order to preserve a model choice the constraints already ruled against. The modest on-device model meets the requirement without the convoy.
distractors.D: Fine-tuning adapts what a model knows; it does not make the model's reasoning accountable. A fine-tuned foundation model is as hard to explain to a regulator as the base model it came from.

questions.question: A grocery retail chain is standing up its first demand-prediction project and wants the work plan to follow the AI/ML pipeline. Which sequence places the stages in the right order?

options.A: Exploratory data analysis, then data pre-processing and feature engineering, then model training with hyperparameter tuning, then evaluation, then deployment, then monitoring
options.B: Feature engineering first on the raw sales data, then data pre-processing to clean the engineered features, then exploratory data analysis to check the result, then training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring
options.C: Data pre-processing, then model training, then deployment, with evaluation performed on live store traffic after release, then monitoring
options.D: Exploratory data analysis, then data pre-processing, then feature engineering, then model training, then evaluation, then deployment, with the pipeline complete once the model ships

rationale.correct: The AI/ML pipeline runs in a stable order: exploratory data analysis reveals what the data holds, data pre-processing cleans it, feature engineering converts it into informative inputs, model training and hyperparameter tuning fit the model, evaluation judges it against held-out data, deployment releases it, and monitoring watches it in production. Each stage feeds the next, and monitoring is a stage of the pipeline, not an optional afterthought.

distractors.B: Engineering features from raw, uncleaned data slips two stages out of order: pre-processing exists so that features are built from reliable inputs, and exploratory data analysis belongs before both, not as a check afterward.
distractors.C: Releasing first and evaluating on live traffic replaces controlled evaluation with an experiment on real customers. Evaluation against held-out data exists precisely so quality is measured before shoppers are exposed to the model.
distractors.D: Ending at deployment omits monitoring, and a demand model degrades as shopping patterns drift. A pipeline that stops when the model ships has no way to notice the day the model stops working.

questions.question: A wildlife conservation nonprofit with two engineers and a six-week grant window needs to identify animal species in camera-trap photos. It holds 1,200 labeled photos. How should the team obtain its model?

options.A: Start from an open source pre-trained model and adapt it to the species set, accepting less task fit and less control in exchange for saving the time, data, and compute of training a custom model
options.B: Design and train a custom model from scratch on the 1,200 photos, so the architecture is purpose-built for camera-trap imagery from the first layer
options.C: Delay the build and spend the grant period collecting and labeling a larger photo set, since a custom model will need far more than 1,200 examples
options.D: Contract a specialist lab to develop a proprietary model after this grant cycle, when a future budget can fund a longer engagement

rationale.correct: Where a model comes from is a trade: reusing an open source pre-trained model saves the time, data, and compute that training a custom model demands, at the price of less task fit and less control. Two engineers, six weeks, and 1,200 labeled photos is precisely the profile that trade favors — the pre-trained model already carries general visual capability, and the small labeled set adapts it to the species involved.

distractors.B: A from-scratch build is machinery the constraints cannot support: purpose-built architecture demands data and compute this team does not have, and 1,200 photos is orders of magnitude short of training visual capability from nothing.
distractors.C: More examples answers the wrong question. The shortage is not data for a custom build; it is that a custom build is the wrong route entirely when a pre-trained model reaches the goal with the photos already in hand.
distractors.D: Pushing the work to a future budget spends the six-week window producing nothing, when the reuse route fits inside it. The grant funds an outcome this cycle, and deferral converts an achievable project into a postponed one.

questions.question: At a franchise restaurant chain, one senior engineer retrains the sales-prediction model on his laptop, deploys it by copying files to the server, and keeps no record of experiments or versions. He has resigned with four weeks' notice. What should the engineering director institute?

options.A: MLOps as a working discipline: experimentation tracking, repeatable processes, scalable systems, managed technical debt, and production readiness, so the workflow survives any individual
options.B: A license for a leading MLOps platform, since adopting the market's standard toolchain will close the gap the departure exposes
options.C: A second engineer hired now to shadow the current one for the remaining four weeks and absorb the workflow before he leaves
options.D: A detailed runbook documenting the current laptop-based workflow step by step, written by the departing engineer during his notice period

rationale.correct: MLOps is a discipline of repeatability — experimentation you can track, repeatable processes, scalable systems, managed technical debt, production readiness — rather than a particular toolchain. The exposure here is that the process lives in one person's habits: nothing is versioned, nothing is reproducible, and departure is the failure mode. Instituting the discipline makes the workflow a property of the organization instead of the individual.

distractors.B: A platform purchase treats the visible symptom and leaves the practice untouched: a tool nobody has wrapped in tracked experiments and repeatable process reproduces the same one-person workflow with a more expensive interface.
distractors.C: A second head absorbs habits, not process. Shadowing transfers the fragility to two people instead of one, and four weeks of observation cannot substitute for versioning, tracking, and reproducibility.
distractors.D: Documenting an unrepeatable workflow labels the problem without fixing it: the runbook describes steps that depend on one laptop's state and one person's judgment, which is disclosure of the defect rather than its removal.

questions.question: A mortgage origination firm's approval-risk model scored 91% accuracy at launch. Over 18 months, as interest rates moved sharply, accuracy has slid to 76%. The code and the model file are confirmed unchanged since launch. What explains the decline, and what is the durable response?

options.A: Production applications have drifted away from the data the model was trained on; institute model monitoring that feeds scheduled or triggered model re-training so the model tracks the changing population
options.B: The decision threshold has become miscalibrated; adjust the approval cutoff until the reported approval rates return to their launch-era levels
options.C: The model's weights have degraded through repeated use in production; restore the original artifact from backup to recover the launch accuracy
options.D: The model has too little capacity for the problem; replace it with a substantially larger model so future economic shifts are absorbed by headroom

rationale.correct: A deployed model degrades when production data drifts from what it was trained on — 18 months of sharp rate movement changed who applies and what risk looks like, while the model stood still. The durable response is the loop: model monitoring to detect the drift as it happens, feeding scheduled or triggered model re-training so the model relearns the current population rather than the launch-era one.

distractors.B: Moving the cutoff can restore the look of launch-era approval rates while the underlying scores remain wrong for today's applicants. The number moves; the mismatch between training data and production data stays.
distractors.C: Weights do not wear out: a model file read a million times is bit-for-bit the file that was deployed, and the stem confirms it is unchanged. Restoring an identical artifact changes nothing.
distractors.D: Capacity is not the gap — the model fit its training distribution well at 91%. A larger model trained on the same outdated data learns the same outdated world, more expensively.

questions.question: A pet insurance company is rolling out a claims classifier that flags likely fraudulent claims for review. About 2% of claims are fraudulent, and a missed fraudulent claim costs roughly 40 times as much as an unnecessary manual review. The board wants model quality tracked and also wants to know whether the system pays off. Which measurement pairing fits?

options.A: Recall on the fraud class as the model-performance metric, since the error cost concentrates on missed fraud, paired with return on investment as the business metric
options.B: Accuracy across all claims as the model-performance metric, with cost per user added later once the rollout has matured enough to measure
options.C: Recall on the fraud class as the model-performance metric, paired with customer feedback gathered in the company's annual satisfaction survey as the business measure
options.D: F1 score on its own, since it balances precision and recall in one number and thereby removes the need to track a separate business metric

rationale.correct: Evaluation has two halves: a model-performance metric picked for the task and its error costs, and a business metric that measures value. With fraud at 2% of claims and a miss costing roughly 40 times a review, the error cost sits on false negatives, which is what recall on the fraud class measures. Return on investment then answers the board's second question — whether the reviews the model triggers cost less than the fraud it catches.

distractors.B: With fraud at 2% of claims, accuracy is the mismatched metric: a model that flags nothing at all is still correct on nearly every claim while missing every fraudulent one. Accuracy rewards exactly the failure this system exists to prevent.
distractors.C: The model half is right, but an annual survey is a lagging signal from the wrong population: claimants' satisfaction moves long after fraud losses do, and it cannot tell the board whether the system pays off.
distractors.D: One blended score covers only the model half. F1 also weighs precision and recall equally when this task's costs are 40-to-1 asymmetric, and no model metric, however balanced, can answer the value question the board asked.

questions.question: A legal e-discovery platform is sizing an LLM workload. Contract documents average 9,000 words, the candidate model's context window is quoted in tokens, and the provider bills by usage. The team is drafting its capacity and cost plan. Which understanding should drive the plan?

options.A: Plan in tokens: the model reads and generates tokens, so whether a document fits the context window and what a call costs are both counted in tokens, and a 9,000-word contract occupies more than 9,000 of them
options.B: Plan in words: for English text, words and tokens correspond one to one, so the existing word counts can stand in for token counts without conversion
options.C: Plan in characters: language models bill by the character, so the platform's stored character counts are the figures the budget should be built on
options.D: Treat unit economics as a post-launch concern, since real invoices will reveal the cost structure more accurately than any estimate made now

rationale.correct: A token is the unit a language model reads and generates, and both the context window and usage are counted in tokens rather than words or characters. Tokens are sub-word units, so a 9,000-word contract occupies noticeably more than 9,000 of them, which is exactly the kind of gap that breaks a capacity plan built on word counts.

distractors.B: Words and tokens do not correspond one to one: tokenizers split many words into several tokens, so word-count planning systematically undersizes both the context budget and the bill.
distractors.C: Characters are the neighboring unit, not the billing one. A plan keyed to character counts measures the wrong quantity at every step, from window fit to per-call cost.
distractors.D: Token economics are a design input, not an accounting afterthought: prompt and document handling decisions made now determine the invoices later, and waiting for real bills means designing blind.

questions.question: A patent law practice is building semantic search over 80,000 filings so attorneys can find conceptually similar passages, not just shared wording. A junior architect asks how the retrieval layer actually finds passages that mean the same thing. Which explanation is correct?

options.A: Chunking splits each filing into retrievable pieces, each piece is encoded as an embedding vector that captures its meaning, and a query is embedded the same way, so conceptual similarity becomes geometric distance between vectors
options.B: Each filing should be embedded whole as a single vector, since chunking is an implementation convenience that adds complexity without changing what the search can find
options.C: The passages are clustered under topic labels assigned during ingestion, and retrieval walks the topic tree from broad categories down to the matching leaf
options.D: Retrieval quality depends mainly on how much text each vector carries, so chunks should be made as large as the embedding model accepts

rationale.correct: An embedding encodes meaning as a vector, which turns similarity of meaning into geometric distance: passages about the same concept sit near each other in vector space even when they share no wording. Chunking splits documents into the retrievable pieces that get embedded, and the size of those pieces shapes what can be found — a chunk is the unit of retrieval, not a storage detail.

distractors.B: Removing chunking removes the granularity retrieval depends on: one vector for an entire filing blurs together everything the filing discusses, so no single passage can be found by its own meaning.
distractors.C: Topic trees are a neighboring retrieval idea, but they are not how embedding-based search works: there are no assigned labels to walk, only distances between vectors in a shared space.
distractors.D: Bigger chunks pack more content into each vector and thereby dilute it: the vector averages over more ideas, and the specific passage an attorney needs becomes harder to isolate. Chunk size is a structural choice, not a capacity to maximize.

questions.question: A consumer electronics support team spent two weeks rewriting its assistant's instructions and worked examples, and troubleshooting replies improved sharply. A director, assuming the model was retrained, asks what the training run cost. Which statement correctly characterizes what the team did?

options.A: The team practiced prompt engineering, shaping the model's behavior through the input alone; no weights changed, which is what separates prompting from every form of tuning, and no training run occurred
options.B: The team performed a lightweight form of fine-tuning, differing from a full training run only in degree, so a small training cost was in fact incurred
options.C: The team practiced context engineering, changing which retrieved documents and history enter the model's context at call time
options.D: The team's gains will need training-scale compute to sustain, since improvements made at the prompt level require moving to model training as usage grows

rationale.correct: Prompt engineering shapes model behavior through the input alone — instructions, wording, worked examples — while the model's weights stay untouched. That is the line that separates it from fine-tuning and every other form of tuning: no training run happened, so there is no training cost to report. The improvement lives in the prompt, not in the model.

distractors.B: Fine-tuning changes weights through a training process; rewriting instructions changes nothing but the input. The two are different in kind, not degree, and conflating them is how phantom training costs appear in budgets.
distractors.C: Context engineering assembles and prioritizes what enters a model call — retrieved content, history, instructions as a payload. This team rewrote the instruction text itself, which is the neighboring discipline of prompt engineering.
distractors.D: Prompt-level improvements do not decay into a compute bill: the prompt is supplied on every call at no training cost, regardless of scale. Nothing about growing usage converts prompting into training.

questions.question: An apparel e-commerce company is scoping five generative AI features. Each needs a model family suited to its inputs and outputs. For each feature, select the model family that fits. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Generate polished product descriptions from bullet-point garment specifications supplied by merchandisers.
Produce photorealistic lifestyle images of garments for campaign mockups before any photo shoot is booked.
Answer customer support questions that arrive with an uploaded photo of a damaged item plus the order's text history.
Draft empathetic replies to written customer reviews for a human agent to approve.
Create style variants of an existing product image, changing color and background while keeping the garment recognizable.

rationale.correct: A foundation model's family is chosen by modality. Text in and text out — specifications becoming descriptions, reviews becoming reply drafts — is the home ground of transformer-based large language models. Image generation, whether creating lifestyle scenes from nothing or producing controlled variants of an existing shot, is what diffusion models do. The support feature is the discriminating case: its input spans two modalities at once, a photo and the order's text history, and a model that must read across input types is a multi-modal model rather than a language-only or image-only one.

questions.question: A digital news publisher has budget for one AI project this year and four candidates on the table. The selection committee wants the project where generative AI specifically earns its place. Which candidate is the strongest GenAI fit?

options.A: A conversational subscriber assistant that answers questions across any section and drafts personalized summaries of long investigations, adapting to topics a rule system would need rewriting for
options.B: A pipeline that reproduces scanned archive pages as text with exact fidelity, since a generative model can recreate each historical page faithfully
options.C: A churn-risk scorer that predicts which subscribers will cancel next quarter from their billing and reading history
options.D: A paywall pricing engine, chosen because it is the candidate the board would find most impressive at the annual shareholder briefing

rationale.correct: A GenAI use case is recognized by the new artifact it produces and by the capabilities that make it fit: summarization, conversation, and the ability to generate content, carried by adaptability and responsiveness where rule systems would need rewriting. The subscriber assistant produces new artifacts — answers and summaries — across shifting topics, which is precisely the profile that justifies a generative model.

distractors.B: Exact-fidelity reproduction is the opposite of generation: a generative model samples plausible output rather than guaranteeing a faithful copy, so the one property this project needs is the one the approach does not offer.
distractors.C: Churn scoring is classic predictive machine learning over labeled history. It produces a probability, not a new artifact, and nothing about it requires the content-generating capabilities the committee is funding.
distractors.D: Boardroom impressiveness is a criterion from outside the decision framework. It says nothing about whether generation, adaptability, or conversational capability are what the project actually exercises.

questions.question: A community bank is planning its first foundation-model deployment for a lending-assistant pilot, and the program manager must lay the FM lifecycle out in the project plan. Which ordering of stages is correct?

options.A: Data selection, then model selection, then pre-training, then fine-tuning, then evaluation, then deployment, then feedback flowing back into the next iteration
options.B: Data selection, then model selection, then pre-training, then fine-tuning, then deployment, with evaluation replaced by feedback gathered from live users after release
options.C: Model selection, then fine-tuning, then pre-training to broaden the tuned model, then evaluation, then deployment, then feedback
options.D: Data selection, then model selection, then pre-training, then fine-tuning, then evaluation, then deployment, with the lifecycle complete once the assistant ships

rationale.correct: The FM lifecycle runs data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, and feedback, and each stage owes its output to the next: data and model choices precede any training, pre-training builds general capability before fine-tuning specializes it, evaluation gates deployment, and feedback closes the loop into the next iteration.

distractors.B: Live user feedback complements evaluation; it cannot replace it. Skipping the evaluation stage turns the bank's real lending customers into the test set, discovering quality problems only after they have consequences.
distractors.C: Pre-training builds the broad capability that fine-tuning then adapts; running fine-tuning first inverts the two stages, and the later pre-training pass would wash out the very specialization the tuning added.
distractors.D: A lifecycle that ends at deployment has no feedback stage, and feedback is what tells the next iteration what to fix. Shipping is a stage boundary, not the finish line.

questions.question: A food delivery marketplace runs a GenAI order-support assistant. Costs are climbing on two fronts: prompts average 6,000 input tokens against about 400 output tokens, and every evening the assistant hits the on-demand request limits and throttles during the dinner peak. What should the team change?

options.A: Treat prompt length as a design decision under token-based pricing and trim the 6,000-token prompts, and move the predictable dinner peak onto provisioned throughput, since the throttling is a load problem rather than a model-quality problem
options.B: Distill the model into a smaller one so each call costs less, letting the evening throttling subside as the per-call footprint shrinks
options.C: Cap the assistant's maximum output length during evening hours, cutting spend where the generation happens
options.D: Re-index the assistant's knowledge base hourly instead of nightly, so fresher retrieved context keeps prompts from growing

rationale.correct: GenAI economics has two levers here, one per symptom. Under a token-based pricing model, prompt and output length are cost decisions, and prompts averaging 6,000 on the input side against about 400 on the output side say the spend concentrates on the input, which prompt design can cut. Provisioned throughput versus on-demand inference is the lever when load, not model quality, is the problem — and a predictable dinner peak that hits on-demand limits is exactly that case.

distractors.B: Distillation is a customization move that changes the model when nothing about the model is wrong. Cheaper calls do not lift an on-demand request limit, so the dinner-peak throttling survives the swap.
distractors.C: Output runs at about 400 against 6,000 of input: capping the small side trims the margin while the dominant cost driver — prompt length — is untouched, and the throttling is not addressed at all.
distractors.D: Refresh frequency governs how current retrieved content is; it neither shortens prompts nor raises request limits. Re-indexing hourly changes a schedule, not either mechanism behind the two symptoms.

questions.question: A travel visa processing assistant has polished, well-tested instruction text, yet it keeps answering from whatever happens to fit in the call: long conversation history crowds out the current rule bulletin, and the applicant's prior-application records are never included at all. Which discipline addresses this failure?

options.A: Context engineering: deciding what goes into each model call — the retrieved records, the history, the instructions — and how those pieces are prioritized when they compete for space
options.B: Prompt engineering: sharper instruction wording that directs the model to give the rule bulletin precedence and to consult the applicant's prior records
options.C: Fine-tuning on historical case decisions, so the model carries the rules in its weights and no longer depends on what reaches the call
options.D: A model with a much larger context window, so that history, bulletins, and records all fit and nothing needs to be prioritized

rationale.correct: The failure is in what reaches the model, not in how the instructions are worded and not in the weights — which is context engineering's territory: assembling and prioritizing the content of each model call, including retrieved records, conversation history, and instructions. The bulletin losing to old history and the records never arriving are assembly and prioritization defects, distinct from prompt wording and from any form of tuning.

distractors.B: Instruction wording cannot include a record that was never assembled into the call. Prompt engineering is the neighboring discipline; it shapes how the model treats what arrives, not what arrives.
distractors.C: Tuning bakes in yesterday's rules: visa bulletins change, and weights cannot be retrained per bulletin. The problem is call assembly, and swapping in a training-time fix leaves that mechanism broken.
distractors.D: A larger context window postpones the collision without resolving it: content still competes, priority is still undefined, and the records that are never fetched still never arrive. Capacity does not substitute for assembly.

questions.question: A smart building management platform currently makes a single FM call: given a work-order description, the model drafts a response for a technician. The team now wants an agent that resolves a fault end to end — looking up the device, adjusting settings through the building-control API, and remembering what it has already tried across a multi-day incident. Which TWO capabilities distinguish the agent they need from the single FM call they have? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Tool usage, so the agent can act on external systems such as the building-control API instead of only generating text about them
options.B: Memory management, so the state of a multi-day incident persists across steps instead of vanishing between calls
options.C: A larger context window, since agent behavior emerges once the model can read enough information in a single call
options.D: A longer request timeout, so that multi-step work can complete inside one extended API call
options.E: Fine-tuned weights, because a model must be retrained on the building's data before it can interact with external systems

rationale.correct: What an agent adds beyond a single FM call is exactly what this fault-resolution job needs: tool usage to act on the world rather than describe it, memory management to persist state across a multi-day incident, and workflow orchestration to sequence the steps. Of the options offered, tool usage and memory management are the two agentic building blocks — the building-control API is a tool to call, and the incident's history is state to manage.

distractors.C: Reading more text per call does not create the ability to act or to persist state. A window is capacity for input, and no amount of it turns a text generator into something that adjusts a damper or remembers yesterday.
distractors.D: A timeout is a serving configuration. Stretching one call longer changes when the call fails, not what the model can do during it — no tools, no memory, no orchestration appear.
distractors.E: Interacting with external systems is granted by tooling, not by training: fine-tuned weights change what the model knows and how it responds, and a tuned model with no tool access still cannot touch the building-control API.

questions.question: A cargo logistics firm's single booking agent now handles rate quoting, customs paperwork, and vessel scheduling. Its prompt has grown unwieldy and errors are crossing between task types. The architects are weighing a move to multiple agents. What do multi-agent system patterns and multi-agent communication patterns actually govern?

options.A: System patterns divide the work among specialized agents — quoting, customs, scheduling — and communication patterns govern how those agents coordinate and hand work off to each other
options.B: They describe running multiple copies of the same generalist agent behind a load balancer, so the main effect of going multi-agent is higher request capacity
options.C: They apply only after the single agent's error rate has doubled, so the right move is to defer any split until operations reach that threshold
options.D: They add process where none is needed: keeping one agent with a sectioned mega-prompt achieves the same separation with less machinery

rationale.correct: Multi-agent system patterns are about structure: dividing work among specialized agents so each carries a focused role such as quoting, customs, or scheduling. Multi-agent communication patterns are the second half — how those agents coordinate and hand off, which is what keeps a divided system coherent. The firm's symptoms, a bloated prompt and errors crossing task types, are precisely what specialization plus governed handoffs address.

distractors.B: Replicating one generalist behind a load balancer is fleet scaling, not multi-agent structure: every copy still carries the bloated prompt and the cross-task errors, just at higher volume.
distractors.C: The symptoms that justify the split are already present. Waiting for a doubled error rate compounds a known structural problem while the trigger threshold does nothing to fix it.
distractors.D: The sectioned mega-prompt is the design that produced the errors: sections share one context and leak into each other. Removing the structural split keeps exactly the coupling the patterns exist to remove.

questions.question: A telecom field-services assistant must reach ticketing, parts inventory, and crew scheduling systems built by three different vendors, and every integration so far has been hand-built. An architect proposes adopting the Model Context Protocol (MCP). What is MCP?

options.A: An open protocol that connects agents and assistants to external tools and data sources through a standard interface, replacing per-vendor custom integrations
options.B: The scheduling component of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that assigns incoming work orders to whichever agent has capacity
options.C: A prompting technique that packs each tool's documentation into the context so the model can imitate calls to that tool
options.D: A network transport standard that encrypts traffic between the assistant and each vendor system it connects to

rationale.correct: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that gives agents and assistants a standard interface to external tools and data sources. Its value is exactly the situation described: instead of one hand-built integration per vendor system, each system exposes its capability through the protocol once, and any MCP-capable assistant can connect. It is a connectivity standard, not a product feature, a prompting trick, or a security layer.

distractors.B: Assigning work orders to agents is an orchestration capability of an agent platform, a different job entirely. MCP standardizes how an agent reaches tools; it does not schedule or route work.
distractors.C: Packing documentation into the context produces imitation, not connection: the model can describe a call it cannot make. MCP is a real interface through which tools are actually invoked.
distractors.D: Encryption in transit is a transport-layer concern that any of the integrations would need regardless. MCP operates at the application layer, defining how tools are exposed and called, not how packets are protected.

questions.question: An online tutoring marketplace's assistant recommends practice books to parents. Support tickets show it confidently citing textbook titles, authors, and page counts for books that do not exist. The engineering lead has filed it as a rare bug to be patched. What is the correct reading of this behavior?

options.A: This is hallucination — fluent, confident output that is wrong — a first-class GenAI failure mode that the design must plan controls around, not an occasional defect to patch case by case
options.B: This is a corrupted model artifact producing garbled facts, so redeploying the model file from a clean backup will restore correct behavior
options.C: This is acceptable if disclosed, so the fix is a notice in the interface stating that book recommendations may contain inaccurate titles
options.D: This is a user-expectation problem, so the fix is asking parents to verify titles in a bookstore catalog before purchasing

rationale.correct: Hallucination is inherent to how generative models work: they produce fluent, confident output that can be wrong, and invented titles with plausible authors and page counts are its signature. Because it is a first-class failure mode rather than an occasional bug, the response is designed-in controls — grounding recommendations in a real catalog, validating output before display — sized to the harm inaccuracy causes here.

distractors.B: A corrupted artifact would degrade behavior broadly and reproducibly, not generate coherent, well-formed, wrong citations. Redeploying the same model restores the same failure mode, because the mechanism is the model.
distractors.C: A notice tells parents the output may be wrong and then keeps showing them wrong output. Disclosure has a place, but it is not the control that stops fabricated titles from reaching users.
distractors.D: Sending parents to verify the assistant's claims converts the system's failure into the customer's chore. The defect is in the product's output, and the burden of catching it cannot be assigned to its users.

questions.question: A freight brokerage runs the same extraction prompt over each carrier's rate email twice — once in the booking flow, once in the audit flow. Reconciliation intermittently fails because the two runs of the same prompt on the same email disagree. Engineers suspect flaky infrastructure. What is actually happening, and what is the durable fix?

options.A: This is nondeterminism: the same prompt need not return the same answer, so a workflow that assumes a repeatable output is broken by design — run the extraction once and have both flows consume the single stored result
options.B: This is transient infrastructure noise: add automatic retries that re-run the extraction until the booking and audit results agree with each other
options.C: This is a sampling configuration issue: set the temperature to zero, which will make the two runs match and restore the workflow's assumption
options.D: This is a known reconciliation quirk: record in the operations runbook that extracted quotes may differ between the two flows so analysts can waive the mismatches

rationale.correct: Nondeterminism is a stated property of generative models: the same prompt on the same input need not reproduce the same answer, and any workflow built on the assumption that it will is broken by design rather than by infrastructure. The durable fix removes the assumption — extract once, store the result, and let booking and audit consume the same artifact, so agreement is guaranteed by construction and not hoped for run to run.

distractors.B: Retrying until two probabilistic runs happen to agree treats the visible mismatch while leaving the design assumption in place; it spends compute to manufacture coincidence and still fails on the days coincidence is slow to arrive.
distractors.C: Lowering the temperature narrows sampling variability; it does not grant a guarantee of identical output, and the workflow's correctness would still hang on a configuration value doing what no configuration promises.
distractors.D: Documenting that the flows disagree converts a design defect into an operating procedure: every waived mismatch is unverified data flowing into audit, with the underlying assumption still broken.

questions.question: A regional airline is selecting a foundation model for a crew-scheduling assistant. Gate-side kiosks need answers within 2 seconds, union data-handling rules require processing to stay in-region, and finance has capped the per-query budget. The model currently leading public capability rankings meets none of the three. How should the selection be made?

options.A: Filter first on the binding constraints — the 2 seconds of latency headroom, the in-region compliance rule, and the per-query cost cap — then choose the most capable model among those that pass, since no single score decides a multi-constraint selection
options.B: Choose the model leading the public capability rankings, since the strongest general performer will compensate for shortfalls on the other dimensions over time
options.C: Score every candidate on cost alone, since one clear, comparable criterion produces a more defensible decision than juggling several incommensurable ones
options.D: Choose the model from the vendor that offered the airline preferential partnership pricing, since commercial alignment matters more than marginal capability differences

rationale.correct: Foundation-model selection is a multi-constraint decision: capabilities, cost, latency, compliance, and model complexity all bear on it, no single score decides, and the binding constraint filters first. A model that cannot answer inside 2 seconds, cannot process in-region, or cannot fit the query budget is ineligible regardless of ranking; among the models that satisfy all three constraints, capability then earns its place as the tie-breaker.

distractors.B: A public ranking is a measurement of a different question — general capability on benchmark tasks — and a top rank cannot compensate for failing a hard latency, compliance, or cost constraint even slightly.
distractors.C: Collapsing the decision to cost is simpler and wrong: the cheapest model that violates the in-region rule or the kiosk latency budget fails the airline exactly as thoroughly as the most expensive one.
distractors.D: Partnership pricing is a criterion from outside the engineering decision. It can tilt a choice between models that already satisfy the constraints; it cannot make an ineligible model eligible.

questions.question: An event ticketing marketplace with no ML infrastructure wants to build a customer-facing GenAI assistant: choose among foundation models from several providers, ground answers in its own help content, and apply content safeguards — all without managing training or serving infrastructure. Which AWS building block fits?

options.A: Amazon Bedrock, the managed platform offering a catalog of foundation models with retrieval and safeguard capabilities behind a single API
options.B: Amazon SageMaker AI, the platform for building, training, and deploying the marketplace's own custom models end to end
options.C: Strands Agents, since a GenAI application of this kind is best built agent-first with autonomous task execution from day one
options.D: Open source models self-hosted on GPU instances, avoiding dependence on any managed platform's roadmap and pricing

rationale.correct: Choosing the AWS GenAI building block is a job-matching exercise: Amazon Bedrock is the managed foundation-model platform — a catalog of FMs from multiple providers with knowledge-grounding and safeguard capabilities behind one API — which is exactly the assistant described. Amazon SageMaker AI and SageMaker JumpStart serve custom model work, Amazon Q is the packaged assistant, and Strands Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore serve agent construction; none of those is the requirement here.

distractors.B: Amazon SageMaker AI performs the adjacent, heavier job: building and training custom models. A team with no ML infrastructure asking for provider FMs behind an API is describing the platform above that layer.
distractors.C: Nothing in the requirement needs autonomous multi-step execution: this is a grounded, safeguarded assistant. Reaching for an agent framework first adds machinery the use case has not asked for.
distractors.D: Platform independence is a preference, not a requirement this team stated, and it is purchased by taking on the serving, scaling, and safety work a managed platform exists to remove from a team like this one.

questions.question: A solar installation services company with no ML infrastructure team is choosing between assembling its own GenAI serving stack on rented GPUs and building on a managed GenAI service. Which TWO advantages does the managed service offer this team? (Select TWO.)

options.A: A lower barrier to entry and faster speed to market, because the platform removes the infrastructure build that the company cannot staff
options.B: Security, compliance, and safety capabilities inherited from the platform, which a self-built stack would have to earn control by control
options.C: Elimination of model inaccuracy, because managed platforms correct hallucinated content before responses are returned to the application
options.D: Full control over model weights and serving internals, letting the team tune every layer of the stack to its workload
options.E: The ability to enforce access rules in the prompt text rather than in platform controls, which keeps the application code simpler

rationale.correct: The managed-platform case rests on two pillars. Commercially, a lower barrier to entry and speed to market: a team without ML infrastructure skips the build entirely and ships while a self-assembled stack is still being racked. Technically, the platform brings inherited security, compliance, and safety — capabilities a self-built stack would have to design, implement, and prove one by one. Cost-effectiveness follows from the same arithmetic for a team this size.

distractors.C: No platform eliminates hallucination: inaccuracy is a property of generative models themselves, and managed services provide safeguard tooling around it, not correction of it. The claimed mechanism does not exist.
distractors.D: Full control of weights and serving internals is the self-hosted stack's advantage, offered here with the sides swapped: the managed trade is precisely giving up that control in exchange for not operating the stack.
distractors.E: Enforcing access rules in prompt text is a control at the wrong layer on either stack: prompts can be steered by crafted input, which is why access enforcement belongs in the platform's control plane, not in instructions.
